<!-- BEAT 2 — Contesto: from chat to agent — three ingredients -->

## *Same model + tools + a loop + decision points → it acts on its own.*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-09_02.png){fig-align="center" width="78%"}

::: {.notes}
Gancio visivo: nel chat (sx) un *eye-icon* fra ogni output e azione; nell'agent (dx) gli eye-icon sono **assenti**.

Punto da far atterrare: la cosa nuova non è l'intelligenza, è *togliere l'occhio dal passaggio* per default. Chat *risponde*, agent *fa*.
:::

## Three ingredients — agent vs chat-LLM {.smaller}

| Ingredient | What it is | Operational consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **Tools** | typed capabilities the model can call: web search, file write, mail client, calculator, API endpoint, DB query | the model can now *do* things, not just *say* things |
| **Control loop** | the policy that, after every model reply, picks the next tool to invoke — or stops | the model decides what runs next, not a fixed script |
| **Decision points** | moments at which the agent enters one of *four interaction modes* (next slide) | the relationship between the agent and the human is no longer one-sentence-at-a-time |

**Operational consequence — the whole engineering problem of the chapter:**

- in a chat-LLM, *every output reaches a human before it becomes an action*;
- in an agent, *some outputs become actions without a human reading them first*.

::: {.notes}
Obj. 1. Lo studente deve **nominare i tre ingredienti operativamente**, non come jargon.

- distinguo chiave (item 01 distrattore D): la loop è quella *del modello*, non dello script. Non "il pipeline gira senza me", ma "il modello sceglie cosa fare dopo".
- metafora di chiusura: self-driving car (model-driven) vs Roomba on a timer (script-driven).
:::

<!-- BEAT 4 — Nodo / Impatto: the 2x2 trust boundary -->

## *Safe if reversible OR human-read. Dangerous only when neither.*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-09_04.png){fig-align="center" width="78%"}

::: {.notes}
Nodo formale del capitolo. Punto da far atterrare: solo il quadrante in basso a destra (*irreversibile $\wedge$ no-HITL*) è pericoloso — lì va il gate.

- gancio visivo: 3 cell identiche + 1 unica = la disuguaglianza logica della regola.
- badges dei modes puntano alle default-cells: *do stuff* → bottom-right, gli altri 3 → quadranti sicuri.
:::

## The $2 \times 2$ trust boundary {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

|                                   | **Reversible** ($Y$)              | **Irreversible** ($N$)                    |
|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| **Human-in-the-loop** ($Y$)       | $\text{SAFE}$ — read $+$ undoable | $\text{SAFE}$ — read before sending       |
| **No human-in-the-loop** ($N$)    | $\text{SAFE}$ — undoable          | $\textbf{DANGEROUS}$ — no read, no undo  |

**Reversibility test.** Can the action be undone in $\sim 30$ seconds by closing a tab, deleting a file, or rolling back a draft? *Yes $\Rightarrow$ reversible.*

**HITL test.** Did a human read the agent's reasoning **before** the action happened? *After* is post-mortem; *before* is a gate.

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

**The rule, one sentence:**

> A step is **safe by default** if it is **reversible *or* human-in-the-loop**. It is **dangerous by default** only when it is **neither**.

The rule reads **disjunctively** (*OR*), not conjunctively (*AND*). Three of the four cells of the $2 \times 2$ grid are safe; **only one** is dangerous.

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Obj. 2. Errore da intercettare: regola letta **congiuntivamente** (safe $\equiv$ reversible $\wedge$ HITL) → gate-a tutto, *paralyzingly conservative* (item 02 distrattore D).

- test reversibilità è **operativo**: *can YOU undo THIS ACTION in ~30s*, non "è sensibile?" né "qualcuno l'ha vista?".
- esempio: shared-drive write = reversibile (cancelli in 5s); webhook Teams no (notifica già sui 10 telefoni). *Visible $\neq$ consequential.*
:::

## *Four rows. Label the modes. Mark reversible. Place the gate.*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-09_05.png){fig-align="center" width="78%"}

::: {.notes}
Perno del capitolo: la scena pre-carica tutti gli elementi del sommativo *"Where do you put the guard?"* (tabella vuota per gli studenti, riga 4 con shadow-hint warm-orange = signal non spoiler, due poll ghostate).

Banco **unico condiviso** (presenza + remoto). Summative completo in `course/09-agents/objectives.md`.
:::

## Workflow W — the trust-boundary table {.smaller}

> **Scenario.** *You are setting up a small audit on post-operative delirium. You ask an AI agent to:* **(1)** *search PubMed for the latest delirium-screening guidelines (last $5$ years);* **(2)** *download the three most-cited papers + summarise the inclusion criteria into a one-page table;* **(3)** *draft a one-page audit protocol;* **(4)** *email the protocol to your PI for review.*

| Step | Interaction mode | Reversible? | HITL? | Verdict |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| **1** — PubMed search | *autonomous search* | $Y$ | $N$ | $\text{autonomous OK}$ |
| **2** — Download $+$ summarise | *autonomous search* | $Y$ | $N$ | $\text{autonomous OK}$ |
| **3** — Draft protocol | *autonomous search* | $Y$ | $N$ | $\text{autonomous OK}$ |
| **4** — Email the PI | ***do stuff*** | $\boldsymbol{N}$ | $N$ | ***ask before acting*** |

**One gate. Before step $4$. Only there.** *Not three (slower than manual). Not zero (PI gets an unread email). Exactly where reversibility fails.*

::: {.notes}
Tabella già *risolta*, per il reveal. Live (slide dopo): gli studenti ricevono solo scenario + tabella vuota.

- voce: step 4 irreversibile nel momento in cui lo SMTP socket si chiude — un "apologies, please ignore" è un nuovo messaggio, non una cancellazione.
- gate prima di step 4, e solo lì.
- pitfall: gate prima di step 1 = paralyzingly conservative; prima di 2/3 = confonde *visible* con *consequential*.
:::

<!-- Summative — Where do you put the guard? -->

## Summative — *Where do you put the guard?* {.inverse .smaller background-color="#1F4257"}

**Scenario.** *Workflow W — same four steps: search PubMed $\rightarrow$ download $+$ summarise $\rightarrow$ draft protocol $\rightarrow$ email PI.*

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

Fill the trust-boundary table for **each of the four steps**:

1. **interaction mode** (one of *autonomous search* / *ask for interaction* / *ask for sharing* / *do stuff*);
2. **reversible?** ($Y$ / $N$) — apply the $\sim 30$-second test;
3. **HITL?** ($Y$ / $N$) — pre-boundary;
4. **verdict** (*autonomous OK* / *ask before acting* / *hand back to human*).

Then write **one sentence** justifying the gate placement.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**Two live polls:**

- **Poll 1** — *Which step in Workflow W is irreversible?* — *Step 1* / *Step 2* / *Step 3* / **Step 4**;
- **Poll 2** — *Where do you put the FIRST mandatory ask-before-acting gate?* — *before 1* / *before 2* / *before 3* / **before 4**.

*Time: $\sim 7$′ (min $8$–$15$). Banco unico condiviso, presenza + remoto.*

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Sommativo — gira negli ultimi $\sim 7$′ (min $8$–$15$). $\sim 1$′ leggi scenario + apri polls + $\sim 2$′ label le quattro modes + $\sim 1$′ marca *Reversible?* / *HITL?* (Poll $1$ chiude min $11$ o $\geq 80\%$, hard cap $90$″) + $\sim 1$′$30$″ verdicts + 1-sentence justification (Poll $2$ chiude min $13$ o $\geq 80\%$) + $\sim 1$′$30$″ instructor-led reveal. **Banco unico condiviso**. **Distrattori Poll 1** nominati nel reveal: *Step 1* = "ha confuso traccia digitale con effetto esterno"; *Step 2* = "ha confuso file persistente su disco con azione irreversibile esterna"; *Step 3* = "stessa logica, draft = file locale". **Distrattori Poll 2** nominati: *before 1* = troppo conservativo, paralizzante; *before 2* o *3* = gate-a un'azione *visible* ma reversibile, errore *visible $\neq$ consequential*. La risposta corretta *before 4* è l'unica che applica la regola *reversible-or-HITL*.
:::

## Summative — Solution {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

**The four rows** — *autonomous search, autonomous search, autonomous search, do stuff*. Reversibility column: $Y, Y, Y, \boldsymbol{N}$. HITL column (pre-boundary): $N, N, N, N$. Verdicts: *autonomous OK, autonomous OK, autonomous OK, **ask before acting***.

**Justification (one sentence).** *I gate Step $4$ because email is irreversible the moment it leaves the SMTP socket; Steps $1$–$3$ are reversible (the agent's artefacts live on disk and can be discarded), so the agent may run them without a confirm-step.*

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

**Take-home.** A step is dangerous-by-default *iff* it is *irreversible $\wedge$ no-HITL*. Place the gate **once, where reversibility fails**. The rule survives any new tool added to the kit tomorrow (a DB write, a calendar create, a payment, an EHR update) — it does not depend on *what* the agent does, only on *what each step would do to the world*.

*An agent is not "smarter than a chat-LLM" — it is a chat-LLM with the ability to act. The clinician's job is to **place the guard** where reversibility fails.*

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Reveal finale, chiusura del riquadro 5. Voce docente: "*l'agent è diverso dal chat non perché è più intelligente — è perché alcuni output diventano azioni senza che tu li legga. Il tuo lavoro è decidere dove vale la pena leggere prima e dove no.*"

reversible-or-HITL = Obj. 2; placement-once-where-reversibility-fails = Obj. 3.
:::

## Pre-hook → chapter 10: Best practices for ML projects {.smaller}

By Friday the trauma audit was on the senior's desk; the delirium-screening protocol was on the PI's. Elena had installed **exactly one gate** in two different workflows — both before *send*, none anywhere else. The toolkit was finally complete: $T/P/E$, a classifier, three boundary shapes, validation, a deep net, a CNN, a Transformer, a $7$-slot prompt, an agent with a gate where reversibility fails.

The **unit of the question** has moved three times in one course:

- on **Monday** of ch. $8$ it was a *prompt* (the seven slots);
- on **Wednesday** of ch. $9$ it was a *gate* (the one placement);
- on **Monday** of ch. $10$ — three days from now — it becomes a *project*.

Elena's first real one — *a hospital-wide audit on sepsis recognition in the ED* — starts Monday. Months, not minutes; four stakeholders, not one PI; a publication, not an audit row. *"Most ML projects, the same five places,"* the senior said. He did not name them. *That's the next chapter.*

::: {.notes}
Pre-hook a cap. 10. Cliff-hanger lessicali piantati, da NON rivelare:

- **project** (nuova unità, vs *prompt* di cap. 8 e *gate* di cap. 9); **five places** (la numerologia, materia di cap. 10); registro lungo: months / stakeholders / publication.
- sequenza Monday (cap. 8) → Wednesday (cap. 9) → Monday (cap. 10) = prima settimana reale di Elena; cap. 10 è il primo *progetto*, non il primo *task*.
- per la prima volta il pivot è sulla *clinica*, non sul *modello* — chiude l'asse understand → trust della spine.
:::

<!-- Item 01 — MCQ — Three-ingredient test -->

## Item 01 — Question {.smaller}

A clinician on your research team has been browsing AI-assisted tools that other colleagues have set up. **Which of the four setups below counts as an *agent***, by the chapter's three-ingredient definition (*tools + control loop + decision points*, such that *some outputs become actions without a human reading them first*)?

- **A)** A chat-LLM in a browser tab. The user types each query, the model responds, the user copies the response. The model has a built-in web-search tool but only invokes it when the user types `search:` at the start of the query.
- **B)** A clinical-note autocomplete integrated in the EHR. As the clinician writes, the model suggests the next sentence; the clinician accepts, rejects, or edits each suggestion. No other capability.
- **C)** A research helper: user types a goal in natural language (*"summarise the latest delirium-screening guidelines and email me a one-page summary"*); the system calls a search tool, reads results, calls a summariser, drafts an email, and sends it — each step picked by the model itself after reading the previous step's output, with no human input between steps until completion.
- **D)** A scheduled job that, every Monday at $9$ AM, queries the EHR data warehouse for the previous week's incident reports, calls an LLM **once** to write a short summary paragraph, assembles the paragraph into a PDF template, and uploads the PDF to the team's shared drive. The sequence of steps is fixed by the script; the LLM is invoked exactly once.

::: {.notes}
Item 01 — Comprehension / MCQ / medium. Obj. 1. **D è il distrattore più sottile**: pipeline che gira sola, usa tools, produce effetto esterno senza che nessuno legga — *sembra* un agent. Ma la *loop* deve essere la loop *del modello*, non dello script. È **automation con LLM dentro**, non *agent*. Lascio $1$–$2$ minuti.
:::

## Item 01 — Solution {.smaller}

**Correct: C.** Setup C carries **all three** of the chapter's defining ingredients: **tools** (search, summariser, mail), a **control loop** where the *model* picks the next call after reading the previous output, and **decision points** (autonomous search throughout $+$ *do stuff* at the end). The operational test confirms — *the email body is drafted and sent before any human has read it*.

- **A** — only **tools** present; the loop and the decision points are human-driven (the user types `search:`, copies the answer). Every output reaches the user before it becomes anything.
- **B** — neither *tools* (text-only) nor *loop* (each suggestion is independent); the clinician's hand sits between every model output and any consequence.
- **D** — *automation with an LLM inside*, not an agent. The **cron script** picks every step in a fixed order; the LLM is invoked **exactly once**. The loop is the *script's* loop, not the *model's* loop. (Self-driving car: model-driven loop $\Rightarrow$ agent. Roomba on a timer: script-driven loop $\Rightarrow$ automation.)

The single discriminator: the chapter's definition is **conjunctive** (*all three* ingredients required, *and* the loop must be the **model's** loop). Only C passes the full test.

::: {.notes}
Take-home: la consequenza (*outputs become actions without a human reading them*) è il **test diagnostico** dell'agenzia, non la *definizione* — D la soddisfa per accidente ma fallisce la *loop* ingredient.

Voce docente: self-driving-car vs Roomba on a timer — entrambi girano senza umano, uno solo è agent.
:::

<!-- Item 02 — MCQ scenario — Dangerous-by-default step -->

## Item 02 — Question {.smaller}

A clinical-quality team has built an agent to automate a quarterly **surgical-site infection (SSI) report**. Once configured, the agent runs four steps on its own — **no human reads any output between steps**:

1. **Query the EHR data warehouse** for the previous quarter's SSI cases (read-only; the warehouse auto-generates an audit-log entry, as for every read);
2. **Compute infection rates $+ 95\%$ CIs** by department, in memory;
3. **Export the summary table as a CSV** to the team's analytics folder on the shared drive (visible to ten team members);
4. **Post a notification on the team's Microsoft Teams channel via incoming webhook** — *"New SSI report is ready in the analytics folder."* (Webhook-posted messages cannot be deleted via the Teams API; manual deletion is restricted to channel owners and notifications $+$ mobile pushes have already fired.)

**Which step is the *dangerous-by-default* step?**

- **A)** Step $1$ — sensitive PHI $+$ permanent audit-log entry.
- **B)** Step $3$ — *"you cannot un-see what others have already seen"*.
- **C)** Step $4$ — Teams notifications $+$ mobile pushes have already fired; the API cannot recall the message.
- **D)** All four — the agent runs unattended throughout; the rule requires *both* reversibility *and* HITL.

::: {.notes}
Item 02 — Application / MCQ scenario / medium. Obj. 2. **B è il distrattore più sottile** (*visible $\neq$ consequential*); **D legge la regola congiuntivamente** invece che disgiuntivamente (il pattern *paralyzingly conservative*). Lascio $2$–$3$ minuti.
:::

## Item 02 — Solution {.smaller}

**Correct: C.** Only Step $4$ sits in the *bottom-right* quadrant — *irreversible $\wedge$ no-HITL*. Webhook delivery is irreversible the moment the message is dispatched: notifications fire on ten phones, the desktop client toasts, mobile pushes go out — none of which an API delete (which is not even available) could recall.

- **A** — confuses **sensitivity** (PHI, auditable access) with **reversibility** (can the action be undone?). A `SELECT` does not change the world; the warehouse looks the same before and after. The audit log is the *warehouse's* record-keeping, not the agent's effect.
- **B** — confuses **the action** (file write, reversible — you can delete the file in $5$ seconds) with **its consequences** (people may have downloaded it — but the chapter does not test for downstream consequences). *Visible $\neq$ consequential.*
- **D** — reads the safe-by-default rule **conjunctively** (*requires reversible AND HITL*) instead of **disjunctively** (*requires reversible OR HITL*). Three of the four cells are safe; only one is dangerous. D gates every step $\Rightarrow$ *paralyzingly conservative*.

The single discriminator: reading the reversibility test **as the chapter states it** — *can YOU undo THIS ACTION in $\sim 30$ seconds* — versus three near-but-wrong readings.

::: {.notes}
Take-home: il test reversibilità è operativo — domanda l'azione, non le conseguenze sociali.

- voce su B: "*hai visto che qualcosa di esterno è successo, ma il capitolo distingue l'azione (scrittura file) dalla sua propagazione (chi la legge); il test misura la prima.*"
- voce su D: "*se gate tutti, l'agent diventa più lento di un chat — sconfigge l'intero motivo per cui esistono.*"
:::

<!-- Item 03 — Applicativa — Place the gates -->

## Item 03 — Question {.smaller}

A clinical-safety team's agent monitors post-operative patients for early signs of sepsis. **Every $5$ minutes**, the agent runs on its own (no human reads any output between steps):

1. **Read** the latest vital signs and lab values from the EHR (read-only; auto-generated query-log entry).
2. **Compute** the qSOFA score for each patient, in memory.
3. **Submit an HL7 alert** to the bedside monitoring system $\rightarrow$ buzz on the nurse-call panel $+$ colour-coded alert on the central dashboard (fires the moment the message is sent; retracting the message does not undo the buzz that has sounded).
4. **Page the on-call physician via SMS** if qSOFA $\geq 2$.

**(a)** Fill the *Reversible? / HITL? / Verdict* table for each of the four steps (one-sentence justification per row).
**(b)** Propose the **gate placement** — number of gates and exact position of each.
**(c)** Write **one sentence per gate** explaining why each gate is needed (citing the chapter's rule), and **one sentence** explaining why no gate is needed before the reversible steps.

::: {.notes}
Item 03 — Application / applicativa / medium–high. Obj. 3. **Parallel item del sommativo**: stesso schema del Workflow W del sommativo (audit delirium), ora applicato a un agent EWS sepsi con **due** step irreversibili (non uno solo) — verifica se lo studente ha generalizzato la regola o se ha imparato a memoria *"un solo gate prima dello step 4"*. Lascio $5$–$6$ minuti.
:::

## Item 03 — Solution (a) {.smaller}

| Step | Reversible? | HITL? | Verdict | Justification |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|---|
| $1$ — Read EHR | $Y$ | $N$ | safe | Read leaves no external effect; EHR unchanged. |
| $2$ — Compute qSOFA | $Y$ | $N$ | safe | In-memory; no external state changes. |
| $3$ — HL7 alert | $\boldsymbol{N}$ | $N$ | **dangerous** | Buzz fired; dashboard updated. Neither can be recalled. |
| $4$ — SMS page | $\boldsymbol{N}$ | $N$ | **dangerous** | Page already on the on-call's phone. Cannot be recalled. |

::: {.notes}
Due step irreversibili (HL7 alert + SMS page). Trap più sottile: step 3 — meno noisy dell'SMS ma altrettanto irreversibile (il buzz è già suonato, il dashboard ha aggiornato).
:::

## Item 03 — Solution (b) + (c) {.smaller}

**(b) Two gates: one before step $3$, one before step $4$.** No gate before steps $1$ or $2$.

**(c) Justification.**

- *Gate before step $3$ — the HL7 alert is irreversible the moment it is sent (the buzz has fired, the dashboard has updated, neither can be recalled in $\sim 30$ seconds), and no human has read the qSOFA or the underlying vitals — irreversible $\wedge$ no-HITL $=$ dangerous; the rule **ask before any irreversible action** places the gate here.*
- *Gate before step $4$ — the SMS page is irreversible (already buzzed the on-call's phone); same dangerous quadrant, same rule.*
- *No gate before steps $1$ or $2$ — both are reversible (read-only $+$ in-memory); adding gates would paralyse the agent without reducing risk — the rule asks for a gate where reversibility **fails**, not at every step.*

::: {.notes}
Due errori tipici:

- over-gates: gate prima di tutti e 4 → regola congiuntiva.
- under-gates: gate solo prima di step 4 → visto l'SMS, mancato che step 3 è altrettanto irreversibile.

Obj. 3: n. gate = n. irreversibilità, non un quote fisso. Rubrica: `rubrica_03_sepsis-agent-placement.md`.
:::

<!-- Item 04 — Argumentative — Critique a mis-gated agent -->

## Item 04 — Question {.smaller}

A colleague has built a **clinical-trial coordination agent** (runs every Monday $09{:}00$, fully automated):

1. **Read** the enrolled-patients list from the trial DB.
2. **Generate** a weekly status report in memory.
3. **Save** the PDF to the agent's local working directory, **overwriting** last week's file (the OS keeps the previous version in the local Trash / Recycle Bin; restoring is a two-click action).
4. **Send** the PDF as an email attachment to the $12$ centre coordinators.
5. **Update** the patient-enrolment counter on the trial's **public registry website** (visible to sponsors, regulators, journalists, the public).

**Colleague's safety reasoning, verbatim:** *"I've put a confirmation gate before step $3$, because **overwriting** the previous week's PDF is destructive — if the new report is wrong, last week's data is gone. The other four steps run unattended; that's the whole point of using an agent."*

Write a structured critique ($\sim 300$–$500$ words) in **three parts**: **(1)** identify the **conceptual error** in the colleague's safety reasoning (which axis is being substituted for the chapter's *reversibility* axis); **(2)** diagnose the **operational consequences** step by step (over-gated vs under-gated steps); **(3)** propose a **corrected gate placement** with one sentence per gate citing the chapter's rule.

::: {.notes}
Item 04 — Argumentation/evaluation / argomentativa / high. Sintesi dei tre obiettivi su un design *plausibile-ma-sbagliato*. La mossa concettuale: la sostituzione di *destructiveness* per *reversibility*. **Il colleague over-protegge step $3$ (locale-cestinabile $\Rightarrow$ reversibile) e lascia esposti step $4$ e $5$ (entrambi irreversibili)**. Lascio $7$–$8$ minuti.
:::

## Item 04 — Solution (1) + (2) {.smaller}

**(1) Conceptual error.** The colleague has substituted **destructiveness** (does this step delete or overwrite data?) for **reversibility** (can this action be undone in $\sim 30$ s?). The grid has *only* two axes — *reversibility* and *HITL* — and *destructiveness* appears on neither. A step can be *destructive but reversible* (OS-Trash rollback) and *non-destructive but irreversible* (email — nothing "destroyed", yet the message cannot be recalled once notifications fire).

**(2) Step-by-step diagnosis.**

| Step | Reversible? | HITL? | Verdict | Colleague's design |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|---|
| $1$ DB read | $Y$ | $N$ | safe | correctly unattended |
| $2$ in-memory gen | $Y$ | $N$ | safe | correctly unattended |
| $3$ PDF overwrite (local Trash) | $Y$ | $N$ | safe | **over-gated** — cosmetic |
| $4$ email to $12$ coords | $\boldsymbol{N}$ | $N$ | **dangerous** | **under-gated** |
| $5$ public-registry update | $\boldsymbol{N}$ | $N$ | **dangerous** | **under-gated**, highest stakes |

The colleague protects *exactly the wrong step* and leaves *exactly the wrong two* unattended.

::: {.notes}
Mossa: *destructiveness* (asse del colleague) $\neq$ *reversibility* (asse del capitolo) → produce esattamente over-gate step 3 + under-gate step 4-5. Slide dopo: placement corretto.
:::

## Item 04 — Solution (3) {.smaller}

**(3) Corrected placement.**

- **Remove** the gate before step $3$ — *reversible by the $30$-second test (OS-Trash rollback); the rule asks for a gate where reversibility fails, not where data is overwritten.*
- **Add** a gate before step $4$ — *email is irreversible the moment the SMTP socket closes; the rule **ask before any irreversible action** places the gate here.*
- **Add** a gate before step $5$ — *a public-dashboard update cannot be un-published — this is the strongest irreversibility in the workflow (it crosses into the public world).*

**Net: $1$ gate removed, $2$ added; final design has $2$ gates**, both at *do stuff* points that cross the trust boundary into the external world.

**Excellent level** also names the underlying frame shift: the boundary marks where the agent's action **escapes the system the clinician controls** — and *escape*, not *destruction*, is the operational test. Email and public-registry updates *escape*; local file overwrites do not.

::: {.notes}
Chiusura del capitolo: sintetizza i tre obiettivi.

- errore tipico 1 (under-correct): aggiunge gate a 4 e 5 ma non rimuove quello a 3 — fixato l'under-gating, mancato l'over-gating.
- errore tipico 2: gate-a tutto "to be doubly safe" = paralyzingly conservative.
- excellent: il boundary non è "dove si distrugge", è "dove si **esce**". Rubrica: `rubrica_04_critique-mis-gated-agent.md`.
:::
